title: Uniform noise stability
statement: A Boolean function class is uniformly noise stable if there is a function assigning a probability $\varepsilon(\delta)\in[0,1]$ to each noise parameter $\delta\in[0,\tfrac12]$, such that $\varepsilon(\delta)$ tends to $0$ as $\delta$ tends to $0$ through positive values, and every function $f$ in the class, in every dimension, has noise sensitivity at parameter $\delta$ at most $\varepsilon(\delta)$ for every $\delta\in[0,\tfrac12]$.
hypotheses_covered: The modulus tends to $0$ as $\delta$ tends to $0$ through positive values
$f$ is a Boolean function on $n$ coordinates
$f$ belongs to the class at dimension $n$
